# Overview {-}

**Question.** Is intrinsic aggregation propensity (Na4vSS, TANGO and WALTZ scores, from `Protein_Aggregation_Master.tsv`) related to which proteins are found in the soluble and insoluble skeletal-muscle fractions of Adult and Old mice, to how they shift between fractions with age, and does this differ between females and males and between GO cellular components?

**What is analysed.**

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| Insoluble fraction, Adult vs Old controls | Protein-level propensity distributions; **Age × Sex** models: Type III HC3-robust `lm` for Na4vSS, aligned-rank-transform (ARTool) models for TANGO and WALTZ |
| Adult soluble starting pool | Proteins detected in at least 2 Adult Control soluble samples **in total across the sexes** (sex does not decide entry); propensity rankings, top-protein plots and a consensus heatmap |
| Fate of high-propensity proteins | Representation in the Adult and Old insoluble fraction, age change in insoluble abundance, and age change in volume-corrected log2(Insoluble/Soluble); sex-specific, at least 2 valid observations per age within sex |
| Propensity vs age effect | Pearson correlation (`cor.test`, two-sided) between propensity and the sex-specific age log2FC; reverse-angle analysis of the strongest shifters |
| GO cellular components | Component-wise Ins/Sol age effects; Adult and Old propensity compared across components (Kruskal–Wallis with Dunn post hoc tests, Holm-adjusted); GO-stratified log2FC correlations |
| Detection-defined propensity | Old-predominant insoluble proteins vs stable proteins: one-sided Wilcoxon, one-sided Fisher (top propensity quartile) and a seeded, component-stratified permutation test; BH-adjusted across the three metrics within sex |

Protein-level *P* values describe differences among detected proteins and their sequence-derived scores; they are not mouse-level biological replication. Detection and propensity scores are not direct evidence of aggregation.

**Outputs** are written under `AOS_CompAgg_v29/`, grouped by analysis class (`InsolubleOverall`, `ProteinLandscape`, `Fate`, `Correlations`, `TopShifters`, `RatioCC`, `GOComponents`, `SolFC`, `DetectionProp`, `QC`); PNG, SVG and CSV files sit side by side. Figures are exported as 600-dpi PNG plus editable SVG, with separate legends.

> **To run:** keep the four input CSV/TSV files (see *Setup*), `OldPredominant_bySex.csv` (from the Adult-vs-Old composition output, `Comp_AO/SexSplit/Detection/`, used by the last analysis section) and the `R/` folder next to this file, then knit. Code is folded by default.

# Setup {-}

Expected input files in the working directory:

- `Aggregates_SampleList_Mesquita.csv`
- `Aggregates_Soluble_raw.csv`
- `Aggregates_Insoluble_raw.csv`
- `Protein_Aggregation_Master.tsv`
- `OldPredominant_bySex.csv` (detection-defined section only)

## Packages

All packages must be installed beforehand (the script stops and lists any that are missing; it no longer installs anything itself). Packages are attached in the same order as in the original analysis, because the order determines which functions mask which.

```{r packages}
pkgs <- c("tidyverse", "rstatix", "car", "ARTool", "ragg", "viridisLite", "patchwork",
          "ggtext", "ggpubr", "ggrepel", "svglite", "cowplot", "AnnotationDbi",
          "org.Mm.eg.db", "GO.db", "knitr", "scales")
missing_pkgs <- pkgs[!vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  stop("Install missing packages first: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}
invisible(lapply(pkgs[1:15], library, character.only = TRUE))
select <- dplyr::select   # AnnotationDbi masks dplyr::select
```

## Figure export settings (presentation only)

**Edit figure sizes only in the `nm_dims` entries below (millimetres).** Entries use the **exact PNG/SVG basename** as panel ID, including the metric and component for every figure, which prevents collisions between metric-specific plots. Every figure is exported as one 600-dpi PNG and one editable SVG, with an independent PNG/SVG legend when applicable. Re-exporting changes only how figures are drawn and saved, never the data or statistics.

After a plotting chunk has run, `list_panels()`, `panel_info("Panel_ID")`, `set_panel_size("Panel_ID", width_mm, height_mm)` and `reexport("Panel_ID")` are available; `export_all_panels()` re-renders every registered figure without rerunning analyses, and `list_configured_panels()` lists all potential panels (including conditional component plots) even before knitting.

```{r nm-inline-figures, echo=FALSE}
# Show every exported figure in the report, right after the chunk that creates it.
# Previews are redrawn from the registered plot objects at screen resolution and embedded
# in the HTML; the 600-dpi PNG/SVG files in the output folders are unchanged.
inline_figures <- TRUE   # FALSE = write figure files only, do not embed previews
inline_dpi     <- 110    # preview resolution (lower = smaller HTML)
inline_zoom    <- 1.5    # on-screen scale relative to the physical panel size
inline_shown   <- character(0)
inline_dir     <- file.path(tempdir(), "inline_figures")
dir.create(inline_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

inline_img <- function(file, width_mm, alt) {
  sprintf('<img alt="%s" src="%s" style="width:%smm; max-width:100%%;"/>',
          alt, knitr::image_uri(file), format(round(width_mm * inline_zoom), trim = TRUE))
}

nm_inline_html <- function() {
  ids <- setdiff(sort(ls(panel_registry)), inline_shown)
  inline_shown <<- c(inline_shown, ids)
  png_fun <- if (exists("save_nm_panel_png")) save_nm_panel_png else save_plot_png
  parts <- vapply(ids, function(id) {
    tryCatch({
      e <- get(id, envir = panel_registry, inherits = FALSE)
      d <- nm_resolve_dims(e$paths[[1]], e$size_key, e$original_width, e$original_height)
      w <- unname(d[["width"]]); h <- unname(d[["height"]])
      leg <- if (isTRUE(e$save_legend)) nm_extract_legend(e$plot) else NULL
      p <- if (!is.null(leg)) nm_set_legend_position(e$plot, "none") else e$plot
      p <- nm_apply_nature_theme(p)
      f <- file.path(inline_dir, paste0(id, ".png"))
      png_fun(p, f, w, h, dpi = inline_dpi)
      html <- paste0("<div style='margin:8px 0 16px 0;'><div style='font-size:80%; font-family:monospace;'>",
                     id, "</div>", inline_img(f, w, id))
      if (!is.null(leg)) {
        ld <- nm_legend_dims[[e$size_key]]
        if (is.null(ld)) ld <- nm_legend_dims[["generic"]]
        fl <- file.path(inline_dir, paste0(id, "_legend.png"))
        save_grob_png(leg, fl, unname(ld[["width"]]), unname(ld[["height"]]), dpi = inline_dpi)
        html <- paste0(html, "<br/>", inline_img(fl, unname(ld[["width"]]), paste(id, "legend")))
      }
      paste0(html, "</div>")
    }, error = function(err) {
      paste0("<p><em>Preview not available for ", id, ": ", conditionMessage(err), "</em></p>")
    })
  }, character(1))
  paste(parts, collapse = "\n")
}

knitr::knit_hooks$set(nm_inline = function(before, options, envir) {
  if (before || !isTRUE(inline_figures)) return(NULL)
  out <- tryCatch(nm_inline_html(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(out) || !nzchar(out)) NULL else paste0("\n\n", out, "\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(nm_inline = TRUE)
```

## Helper functions

```{r general-helpers}
clean_id <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_trim(as.character(x))

  x <- stringr::str_remove(x, "^>")

  x <- dplyr::if_else(stringr::str_detect(x, "\\|"), stringr::str_split_fixed(x, "\\|", 3)[, 2], x)

  x <- stringr::str_remove(x, ";.*$")

  stringr::str_remove(x, "-\\d+$")
}

clean_treatment <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_trim(as.character(x)))

  dplyr::case_when(
    stringr::str_detect(x, "rapa") ~ "Rapamycin",
    stringr::str_detect(x, "exer|^ex$") ~ "Exercise",
    TRUE ~ "Control"
  )
}

read_metric_master <- function(file) {
  if (grepl("\\.csv$", file, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    read.csv(file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    readr::read_tsv(file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  }
}

safe_cor_stats <- function(data) {

  n <- dplyr::n_distinct(data$Protein_ID)

  sx <- stats::sd(data$log2FC, na.rm = TRUE)

  sy <- stats::sd(data$Metric_Score, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (n < 3 || !is.finite(sx) || !is.finite(sy) || sx == 0 || sy == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(n = n, r = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
  }

  z <- stats::cor.test(data$log2FC, data$Metric_Score, method = "pearson")

  tibble::tibble(n = n, r = unname(z$estimate), p = z$p.value)
}
```

# Load data and assign manuscript GO-CC bins

```{r load-and-go-bins}
for (f in c(sample_index_file, raw_file, insoluble_raw_file, aggregation_master_file)) {
  if (!file.exists(f)) {
    stop("Input file not found: ", f)
  }
}

sample_index <- read.csv(sample_index_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

raw_dat <- read.csv(raw_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

aggregation_master <- read_metric_master(aggregation_master_file)

raw_cols <- colnames(raw_dat)

meta <- sample_index %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ID = as.character(ID),
    Sample = dplyr::case_when(ID %in% raw_cols ~ ID, paste0("X", ID) %in% raw_cols ~ paste0("X", ID), TRUE ~ ID),
    Age = stringr::str_to_title(stringr::str_trim(as.character(Age))),
    Sex = stringr::str_to_title(stringr::str_trim(as.character(Sex))),
    Treatment = clean_treatment(Treatment)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample %in% raw_cols)

sample_cols <- intersect(meta$Sample, raw_cols)

if (length(sample_cols) == 0) {
  stop("No metadata sample IDs matched columns in the soluble matrix.")
}

long <- raw_dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein.Group, Genes, dplyr::all_of(sample_cols)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::all_of(sample_cols), names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(meta %>% dplyr::select(Sample, Age, Sex, Treatment), by = "Sample") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Abundance = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Abundance)),
    Detected =
      !is.na(Abundance) &
      Abundance > 0,
    Gene1 = stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_extract(as.character(Genes), "^[^;]+"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(Sex), !is.na(Treatment))

go_cc_offspring <- AnnotationDbi::as.list(GO.db::GOCCOFFSPRING)

get_offspring <- function(go_id) {
  kids <- go_cc_offspring[[go_id]]

  unique(c(go_id, kids))
}

bin_terms <- lapply(
  bin_roots,
  function(ids) {
    unique(unlist(lapply(ids, get_offspring), use.names = FALSE))
  }
)

assign_bin <- function(go_vec) {

  go_vec <- unique(go_vec[!is.na(go_vec)])

  if (length(go_vec) == 0) {
    return("Other/Unassigned")
  }

  for (b in bin_priority) {
    if (any(go_vec %in% bin_terms[[b]])) {
      return(b)
    }
  }

  "Other/Unassigned"
}

genes <- sort(unique(na.omit(long$Gene1)))

gene2entrez <- suppressMessages(
  AnnotationDbi::select(org.Mm.eg.db, keys = genes, keytype = "SYMBOL", columns = c("SYMBOL", "ENTREZID"))
) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(SYMBOL, ENTREZID) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ENTREZID))

entrez2go <- suppressMessages(
  AnnotationDbi::select(

    keys = sort(unique(gene2entrez$ENTREZID)),
    keytype = "ENTREZID",
    columns = c("ENTREZID", "GO", "ONTOLOGY")

) %>%
  dplyr::filter(ONTOLOGY == "CC", !is.na(GO)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(ENTREZID, GO)

gene_bin <- gene2entrez %>%
  dplyr::left_join(entrez2go, by = "ENTREZID") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SYMBOL) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(GO_CC = list(unique(GO)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Bin = vapply(GO_CC, assign_bin, character(1)))

long <- long %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_bin %>% dplyr::select(SYMBOL, Bin), by = c("Gene1" = "SYMBOL")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Bin = dplyr::if_else(is.na(Bin), "Other/Unassigned", Bin))

readr::write_csv(long %>% dplyr::distinct(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin), file.path(nat_dirs$QC, "GO_bin_map.csv"))

metrics_wide <- aggregation_master %>%
  dplyr::transmute(

metrics_long <- metrics_wide %>%

  dplyr::filter(is.finite(Metric_Score)) %>%

detection_counts <- long %>%

eligible_group_ids <- detection_counts %>%

  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(Protein.Group, delim = ";") %>%

    Protein_ID != "",

go_metric_data <- eligible_group_ids %>%

  dplyr::filter(Bin %in% display_bins) %>%

eligible_group_keys <- detection_counts %>%

retained <- long %>%

  dplyr::inner_join(eligible_group_keys, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin", "Age", "Sex", "Treatment")) %>%
```

# Restored Adult–Old insoluble protein-level aggregation propensity

This section restores the **insoluble-fraction intrinsic propensity** panels from the
previous `2.AO_Insol_Agg_v9.Rmd` workflow (not the soluble starting-universe
analyses below). The insoluble raw matrix is filtered **within each Age × Sex ×
Treatment group**: a protein group must have at least 2 detected samples;
UniProt IDs are separated and counted only once per group. Control mice only
are compared between Adult and Old. Each point represents **one unique
protein sequence**, not a biological replicate. TANGO is normalized to
sequence length, while WALTZ is the percentage of amyloid residues.

To preserve the original statistical procedures, Na4vSS is tested with a
**two-factor Age × Sex linear model (Type III, HC3-robust)** and TANGO/WALTZ
with **aligned-rank-transform Age × Sex factorial models** (ARTool). These
protein-level analyses describe differences in the distribution of predicted
sequence properties across detected proteins; their p-values should not be
interpreted as mouse-level biological replication. No p-values are hardcoded:
the models are refitted on the input data at each run.

The three individual panels and the assembled three-metric plot are exported
at the exact dimensions listed under `InsolubleOverall` in the unified Nature
Metabolism helper. Raw statistics, retained protein-level scores, and sample
eligibility diagnostics are saved in `InsolubleOverall/`.

```{r aoi-restored-insoluble-overall, fig.keep="none"}
# This is intentionally separate from the soluble `long`, `retained`, and
# `go_metric_data` objects used in the rest of the manuscript.
aoi_raw <- read.csv(insoluble_raw_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
aoi_required <- c("Protein.Group", "Genes")
if (!all(aoi_required %in% colnames(aoi_raw))) {
  stop("Missing protein-group columns in insoluble input: ",
       paste(setdiff(aoi_required, colnames(aoi_raw)), collapse = ", "))
}
aoi_raw_cols <- colnames(aoi_raw)
aoi_meta <- sample_index %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ID = as.character(ID),
    Sample = dplyr::case_when(
      ID %in% aoi_raw_cols ~ ID,
      paste0("X", ID) %in% aoi_raw_cols ~ paste0("X", ID),
      TRUE ~ ID
    ),
    Age = stringr::str_to_title(stringr::str_trim(as.character(Age))),
    Sex = stringr::str_to_title(stringr::str_trim(as.character(Sex))),

  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample %in% aoi_raw_cols)
aoi_samples <- intersect(aoi_meta$Sample, aoi_raw_cols)
if (!length(aoi_samples)) stop("No sample IDs match the raw insoluble matrix.")

aoi_long <- aoi_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein.Group, Genes, dplyr::all_of(aoi_samples)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::all_of(aoi_samples), names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(aoi_meta %>% dplyr::select(Sample, Age, Sex, Treatment), by = "Sample") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Abundance = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Abundance)),
    Detected = !is.na(Abundance) & Abundance > 0,
    Gene1 = stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_extract(as.character(Genes), "^[^;]+"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(Sex), !is.na(Treatment))

aoi_detection <- aoi_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Age, Sex, Treatment) %>%

aoi_eligible <- aoi_detection %>%

  dplyr::mutate(Protein_ID = clean_id(Protein.Group)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Protein_ID != "",
    !stringr::str_detect(Protein_ID, stringr::regex("^cRAP-", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Age, Sex, Treatment, Protein_ID)

aoi_age_x <- tibble::tibble(
  Group = factor(
    c("Adult Female", "Old Female", "Adult Male", "Old Male"),
    levels = c("Adult Female", "Old Female", "Adult Male", "Old Male")
  ),
  x_pos = c(1.00, 1.40, 2.20, 2.60)
)
aoi_sex_annotation <- tibble::tibble(
  Sex_label = c("Female", "Male"),
  x_mid = c(1.20, 2.40),
  line_label = "─────────────"
)
aoi_age_metric_data <- aoi_eligible %>%
  dplyr::filter(Treatment == "Control", Age %in% c("Adult", "Old")) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(metrics_long, by = "Protein_ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Age = factor(Age, levels = c("Adult", "Old")),
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Metric = factor(Metric, levels = metric_levels),
    Group = factor(paste(Age, Sex), levels = c("Adult Female", "Old Female", "Adult Male", "Old Male"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(aoi_age_x, by = "Group")

# Exact tests from 2.AO_Insol_Agg_v9 (renamed to avoid clashing with GO helpers).
aoi_type3_hc3 <- function(dd) {
  dd <- droplevels(dd)
  if (nlevels(dd$Age) < 2L || nlevels(dd$Sex) < 2L) {
    return(c(Age = NA_real_, Sex = NA_real_, Int = NA_real_))
  }
  contrasts(dd$Age) <- stats::contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Age))
  contrasts(dd$Sex) <- stats::contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Sex))
  fit <- stats::lm(Metric_Score ~ Age * Sex, data = dd)
  a <- car::Anova(fit, type = 3, white.adjust = "hc3")
  pcol <- grep("^Pr\\(", colnames(a), value = TRUE)[1]
  c(Age = as.numeric(a["Age", pcol]), Sex = as.numeric(a["Sex", pcol]), Int = as.numeric(a["Age:Sex", pcol]))
}
aoi_art_factorial <- function(dd) {
  dd <- droplevels(dd)
  if (nlevels(dd$Age) < 2L || nlevels(dd$Sex) < 2L) {
    return(c(Age = NA_real_, Sex = NA_real_, Int = NA_real_))
  }
  fit <- ARTool::art(Metric_Score ~ Age * Sex, data = dd)
  a <- stats::anova(fit)
  get_p <- function(term) {
    idx <- match(term, rownames(a))
    if (is.na(idx)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(a[idx, "Pr(>F)"])
  }
  c(Age = get_p("Age"), Sex = get_p("Sex"), Int = get_p("Age:Sex"))
}

aoi_age_metric_stats <- purrr::map_dfr(metric_levels, function(metric) {
  dd <- aoi_age_metric_data %>% dplyr::filter(Metric == metric)
  p <- if (nrow(dd) < 4L) {
    c(Age = NA_real_, Sex = NA_real_, Int = NA_real_)
  } else if (metric == "Na4vSS") {
    aoi_type3_hc3(dd)
  } else {
    aoi_art_factorial(dd)
  }
  tibble::tibble(Metric = metric, p_Age = p[["Age"]],
                 p_Sex = p[["Sex"]], p_Int = p[["Int"]],
                 Method = if (metric == "Na4vSS") "Type III HC3 linear model"
                          else "Aligned-rank-transform factorial model")
})
readr::write_csv(aoi_detection, file.path(nat_dirs$InsolubleOverall, "AOI_Raw_DetectionCount.csv"))
readr::write_csv(aoi_age_metric_data, file.path(nat_dirs$InsolubleOverall, "AOI_Raw_ProteinMetrics.csv"))
readr::write_csv(aoi_age_metric_stats, file.path(nat_dirs$InsolubleOverall, "AOI_Raw_stats.csv"))
print(aoi_age_metric_stats)

# Figure layout preserves the original four group ordering, colors, violin +
# boxplot + protein-level points, Age/Sex/Int annotations and sex group labels.
aoi_fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), "NA", ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}
aoi_make_age_metric_plot <- function(metric, show_legend = TRUE) {
  st <- aoi_age_metric_stats %>% dplyr::filter(Metric == metric)
  dd <- aoi_age_metric_data %>% dplyr::filter(Metric == metric)
  ggplot2::ggplot(dd, ggplot2::aes(x = x_pos, y = Metric_Score)) +
    ggplot2::geom_violin(
      ggplot2::aes(fill = Age, group = Group),
      trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.55, scale = "width", width = 0.37
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
      ggplot2::aes(fill = Age, group = Group),
      width = 0.14, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.50,
      linewidth = nm_style$data_line
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(shape = Sex),
      position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.05, height = 0),
      size = nm_style$point_small, alpha = 0.55, colour = "black"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = aoi_sex_annotation,
      ggplot2::aes(x = x_mid, y = -Inf, label = line_label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 2.25,
      size = 2.0, colour = "grey35"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = aoi_sex_annotation,
      ggplot2::aes(x = x_mid, y = -Inf, label = Sex_label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 4.0,
      size = 2.0, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey25"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = age_cols, drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = sex_shapes, drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = aoi_age_x$x_pos,
      labels = c("Adult", "Old", "Adult", "Old"),
      limits = c(0.65, 2.95),
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = if (metric == "WALTZ %") "WALTZ %" else metric,
      subtitle = paste0("Age=", aoi_fmt_p(st$p_Age),
                        " | Sex=", aoi_fmt_p(st$p_Sex),
                        " | Int=", aoi_fmt_p(st$p_Int)),
      x = NULL,
      y = metric_y_labels[[metric]],

    ) +
    theme_nm(legend_position = if (show_legend) "right" else "none") +

      axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, r = 2, b = 11, l = 2, unit = "mm")
    )
}

# Single figures for placement in editable manuscript figure layouts.
```

# GO-bin statistical helpers

```{r go-statistical-helpers}
run_kw_dunn <- function(data, grouping_vars) {

  kw <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(grouping_vars))) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(
      function(.x, .y) {

        dd <- .x %>%
          dplyr::group_by(Bin) %>%
          dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Protein_ID) >= min_go_n) %>%
          dplyr::ungroup() %>%
          droplevels()

        if (dplyr::n_distinct(dd$Bin) < 2) {
          return(tibble::tibble(n = nrow(dd), p_KW = NA_real_))
        }

        tibble::tibble(n = nrow(dd), p_KW = stats::kruskal.test(Metric_Score ~ Bin, data = dd)$p.value)
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  dunn <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(grouping_vars))) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(
      function(.x, .y) {

        dd <- .x %>%
          dplyr::group_by(Bin) %>%
          dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Protein_ID) >= min_go_n) %>%
          dplyr::ungroup() %>%
          droplevels()

        if (dplyr::n_distinct(dd$Bin) < 2) {
          return(tibble::tibble())
        }

        tryCatch(
          rstatix::dunn_test(dd, Metric_Score ~ Bin, p.adjust.method = "holm"),
          error = function(e) {
            tibble::tibble()
          }
        )
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  list(kw = kw, dunn = dunn)
}

save_component_fc_figures <- function(plot, plot_data, metric, file_prefix, comparison_label) {

  mtag <- metric_tag(metric)

  metric_dir <- file.path(nat_dirs$SolFC, mtag)

  # Manuscript export: remove the redundant overall title but retain the
  # shared Sex legend here so the Nature helper can export it separately.
  metric_axis_short <- c("Na4vSS" = "Na4vSS", "TANGO" = "TANGO / length", "WALTZ %" = "WALTZ residues (%)")

  plot_svg <- plot +
    ggplot2::labs(title = NULL, x = "Soluble age effect, log2FC", y = unname(metric_axis_short[[metric]])) +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "right")

  save_nat_figure(plot_svg, file.path(metric_dir, paste0(file_prefix, "_", mtag, ".svg")), size_key = "fc_grid")

  component_tags <- c(
    "Sarcomere/Myofibril" = "Sarc",
    "Cytoskeleton" = "Cytosk",
    "Extracellular" = "Extra",
    "ECM" = "ECM",
    "Nucleus" = "Nuc",
    "Mitochondrion" = "Mito",
    "Plasma membrane" = "PM",
    "Cytosol" = "Cytosol"
  )

  for (bin_name in display_bins) {

    dd_bin <- plot_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(as.character(Bin) == bin_name) %>%
      droplevels()

    if (nrow(dd_bin) == 0L) {
      next
    }

    present_sexes <- names(sex_shapes)[names(sex_shapes) %in% as.character(dd_bin$Sex)]

    p_ind <- ggplot2::`%+%`(plot, dd_bin) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Bin_lab, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
      ggplot2::labs(title = paste0(comparison_label, " — ", metric)) +
      ggplot2::guides(
        shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
          override.aes = list(colour = unname(sex_cols[present_sexes]), size = 1.8, alpha = 1)
        )
      )

    component_tag <- unname(component_tags[bin_name])

    if (is.na(component_tag)) {
      component_tag <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", bin_name)
    }

    p_ind_svg <- p_ind +
      ggplot2::labs(title = NULL, x = "Soluble age effect, log2FC", y = unname(metric_axis_short[[metric]])) +
      ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "none")

    save_nat_figure(
      p_ind_svg,
      file.path(metric_dir, paste0(file_prefix, "_", mtag, "_", component_tag, ".svg")),
      size_key = "fc_single",
      save_legend = FALSE
    )
  }

  invisible(metric_dir)
}
```

# Adult soluble protein-level aggregation propensity landscape

This descriptive analysis starts with proteins detected in **at least 2 Adult Control soluble samples in total, regardless of sex**, and asks which individual proteins have the greatest sequence-derived aggregation propensity. Female and male detections are pooled only for defining this starting universe because AGGRESCAN, TANGO, and WALTZ are intrinsic sequence-derived properties rather than sex-specific measurements. Proteins are ranked independently by AGGRESCAN Na4vSS, normalized TANGO score, and WALTZ amyloid percentage. Each protein is represented once. A percentile-based consensus view is also generated to identify proteins that rank highly across more than one metric without averaging the raw metric scales.

```{r adult-soluble-protein-propensity-landscape, fig.keep="none"}
# Number of proteins shown in the manuscript ranked plots.
# Keep this deliberately compact for the main figure.
top_n_plot <- 10
top_n_shift_label <- 5

# Keep a longer metric-specific shortlist as a CSV for follow-up / labeling.
top_n_csv <- 25

# Number selected from the top of each metric to build the consensus heatmap.
top_n_heat <- 15

prop_out_dir <- nat_dirs$ProteinLandscape

dir.create(prop_out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Use the same component palette logic as the GO-component analysis so the
# protein-level plots lead visually into the subsequent cellular-component plots.
adult_all_bins_palette <- sort(unique(as.character(long$Bin[long$Bin != "Other/Unassigned"])))

adult_component_pal_all <- setNames(
  viridisLite::viridis(length(adult_all_bins_palette), option = "D", end = 0.95),
  adult_all_bins_palette
)

adult_component_cols <- adult_component_pal_all[display_bins]

# Adult Control soluble protein universe.
# IMPORTANT: eligibility is intentionally independent of sex because the
# aggregation-propensity scores and the initial protein/component landscape are
# sequence-derived, not sex-specific. A protein group enters the starting pool
# when it is detected in >= 2 Adult Control soluble samples TOTAL across females
# and males. Thus 1 Female + 1 Male qualifies. Sex is introduced only later when
# age-associated outcomes are estimated.
adult_soluble_pool_counts <- long %>%
  dplyr::filter(Age == "Adult", Treatment == "Control", Bin %in% display_bins) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    N_detected_AdultSol = sum(Detected, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_detected_Female = sum(Detected & Sex == "Female", na.rm = TRUE),
    N_detected_Male = sum(Detected & Sex == "Male", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

readr::write_csv(adult_soluble_pool_counts, file.path(prop_out_dir, "AdultSol_pool_detection_audit.csv"))

adult_soluble_ids <- adult_soluble_pool_counts %>%
  dplyr::filter(N_detected_AdultSol >= min_detected) %>%
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(Protein.Group, delim = ";") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Protein_ID = clean_id(Protein.Group), Gene1 = stringr::str_trim(as.character(Gene1))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Protein_ID != "",
    !stringr::str_detect(Protein_ID, stringr::regex("^cRAP-", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Protein_ID, Gene1, Bin) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Gene = {
      z <- Gene1[!is.na(Gene1) & Gene1 != ""]
      if (length(z) > 0) z[[1]] else Protein_ID[[1]]
    },
    Bin = {
      z <- as.character(Bin)[!is.na(Bin)]
      if (length(z) > 0) z[[1]] else "Other/Unassigned"
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Bin %in% display_bins)

adult_propensity <- adult_soluble_ids %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(metrics_wide, by = "Protein_ID") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Na4vSS_rank = dplyr::dense_rank(dplyr::desc(`Na4vSS`)),
    TANGO_rank = dplyr::dense_rank(dplyr::desc(`TANGO`)),
    WALTZ_rank = dplyr::dense_rank(dplyr::desc(`WALTZ %`)),
    Na4vSS_percentile = dplyr::percent_rank(`Na4vSS`),
    TANGO_percentile = dplyr::percent_rank(`TANGO`),
    WALTZ_percentile = dplyr::percent_rank(`WALTZ %`)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Consensus_percentile = mean(c(Na4vSS_percentile, TANGO_percentile, WALTZ_percentile), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Consensus_percentile = dplyr::if_else(is.nan(Consensus_percentile), NA_real_, Consensus_percentile)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::add_count(Gene, name = "Gene_n") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Protein_Label = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(Gene) | Gene == "" ~ Protein_ID,
      Gene_n > 1 ~ paste0(Gene, " | ", Protein_ID),
      TRUE ~ Gene
    )
  )

readr::write_csv(
```

# Fate of high-propensity proteins from the Adult soluble starting pool

The protein-level propensity analysis above defines one fixed **Adult Control soluble starting pool** using detection in at least 2 samples total across females and males. The analyses below then ask what happens to those same proteins with aging. Sex does not affect entry into the starting pool; sex-specific requirements are applied only when an age-associated endpoint is estimated. Three complementary endpoints are used:

1. whether a protein is detectably represented in the Adult or Old insoluble fraction;
2. the age-associated change in insoluble abundance; and
3. the age-associated change in volume-corrected log2(Insoluble/Soluble), which more directly captures a relative shift toward insolubility.

Age effects are calculated separately in females and males. For the sex-specific insoluble-abundance and paired Ins/Sol endpoints, a protein must have at least `min_detected` (=2) valid observations in both Adult and Old within that sex; failure of this downstream estimability criterion does not remove the protein from the underlying Adult-soluble starting pool. Continuous fate tiles use blue-white-red scales centered on zero. An asterisk denotes **raw p < 0.05** only. The existing percentile-rank heatmap is retained separately and uses a viridis scale so that propensity rank and age-associated log2FC are visually distinct quantities.

```{r adult-soluble-fate-data, fig.keep="none"}
# Number of high-propensity proteins shown in the Adult -> Old dumbbell plot.
fate_top_n <- 20

# Volume correction used in the validated solubility/ratio workflow.
# The LC aliquot is 5 uL after a 1:1 loading-buffer dilution, so it represents
# 2.5 uL of the original biochemical fraction. Whole-fraction-equivalent scale
# factors are therefore 150/2.5 = 60 for soluble and 100/2.5 = 40 for insoluble.
# ALL ratio quantities below use these corrected whole-fraction-equivalent values.
ratio_sol_fraction_volume_ul <- 150
ratio_ins_fraction_volume_ul <- 100
ratio_loading_buffer_dilution <- 2
ratio_lc_volume_ul <- 5

ratio_original_fraction_ul_in_lc <-
  ratio_lc_volume_ul /
  ratio_loading_buffer_dilution

ratio_sol_scale_factor <-
  ratio_sol_fraction_volume_ul /
  ratio_original_fraction_ul_in_lc

ratio_ins_scale_factor <-
  ratio_ins_fraction_volume_ul /
  ratio_original_fraction_ul_in_lc

ratio_log2_volume_offset <- log2(ratio_ins_scale_factor / ratio_sol_scale_factor)

cat(
  sprintf(
    paste0("Volume-corrected ratio factors: soluble x%.1f; insoluble x%.1f; ", "log2 offset = %.6f\n"),
    ratio_sol_scale_factor,
    ratio_ins_scale_factor,
    ratio_log2_volume_offset
  )
)

# Read the insoluble raw matrix. The soluble matrix is already available as raw_dat.
insoluble_raw_dat <- read.csv(insoluble_raw_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Build a protein-by-animal table for either biochemical fraction. This uses the
# same sample metadata and protein-ID cleaning used elsewhere in this report.
make_fraction_sample_data <- function(dat, fraction_name) {

  fraction_sample_cols <- intersect(meta$Sample, colnames(dat))

  if (length(fraction_sample_cols) == 0L) {
    stop("No sample columns matched the metadata for fraction: ", fraction_name)
  }

  dat %>%
    dplyr::select(Protein.Group, dplyr::all_of(fraction_sample_cols)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::all_of(fraction_sample_cols),
      names_to = "Sample",
      values_to = "Abundance"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(meta %>% dplyr::select(Sample, Age, Sex, Treatment), by = "Sample") %>%
    tidyr::separate_longer_delim(Protein.Group, delim = ";") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Protein_ID = clean_id(Protein.Group),
      Abundance = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Abundance)),
      Fraction = fraction_name
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Protein_ID != "",
      !stringr::str_detect(Protein_ID, stringr::regex("^cRAP-", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      !is.na(Age),
      !is.na(Sex),
      !is.na(Treatment)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Sample, Protein_ID, Age, Sex, Treatment, Fraction) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      Abundance = if (all(is.na(Abundance))) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE)
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

safe_welch_p <- function(data, value_col) {

  value_col <- rlang::ensym(value_col)

  dd <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(Age %in% c("Adult", "Old"), is.finite(!!value_col))

  n_adult <- sum(dd$Age == "Adult")
  n_old <- sum(dd$Age == "Old")

  if (n_adult < 2L || n_old < 2L) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  out <- tryCatch(
    stats::t.test(
      x = dd %>%
        dplyr::filter(Age == "Old") %>%
        dplyr::pull(!!value_col),
      y = dd %>%
        dplyr::filter(Age == "Adult") %>%
        dplyr::pull(!!value_col),
      var.equal = FALSE
    )$p.value,
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )

  out
}

sol_sample_level <- make_fraction_sample_data(raw_dat, "Soluble") %>%
  dplyr::filter(Treatment == "Control", Age %in% c("Adult", "Old"), Protein_ID %in% adult_propensity$Protein_ID)

ins_sample_level <- make_fraction_sample_data(insoluble_raw_dat, "Insoluble") %>%
  dplyr::filter(Treatment == "Control", Age %in% c("Adult", "Old"), Protein_ID %in% adult_propensity$Protein_ID)

# ── Insoluble detection status ------------------------------------------------
ins_detection <- ins_sample_level %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID, Age, Sex) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    N_detected = sum(is.finite(Abundance) & Abundance > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    Present = N_detected >= min_detected,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

make_detection_code <- function(sexes) {
  sexes <- unique(as.character(sexes))
  has_f <- "Female" %in% sexes
  has_m <- "Male" %in% sexes

  dplyr::case_when(has_f & has_m ~ "F/M", has_f ~ "F", has_m ~ "M", TRUE ~ "—")
}

ins_presence <- ins_detection %>%
  dplyr::filter(Present) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID, Age) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Detection = make_detection_code(Sex), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Age, values_from = Detection, names_glue = "{Age}_Ins")

# ── Age effect on insoluble abundance ----------------------------------------
ins_positive <- ins_sample_level %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(Abundance), Abundance > 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(log2_Abundance = log2(Abundance))

ins_group_mean <- ins_positive %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID, Sex, Age) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Mean_Abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Age, values_from = c(Mean_Abundance, n)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(Mean_Abundance_Adult),
    is.finite(Mean_Abundance_Old),
    Mean_Abundance_Adult > 0,
    Mean_Abundance_Old > 0,
    n_Adult >= min_detected,
    n_Old >= min_detected
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Delta_Ins = log2(Mean_Abundance_Old / Mean_Abundance_Adult))

ins_p <- ins_positive %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID, Sex) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ tibble::tibble(p_Ins = safe_welch_p(.x, log2_Abundance))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

ins_effect <- ins_group_mean %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ins_p, by = c("Protein_ID", "Sex"))

# ── Per-animal log2(Insoluble/Soluble) and age effect ------------------------
ratio_sample <- dplyr::bind_rows(sol_sample_level, ins_sample_level) %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(Abundance), Abundance > 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample, Protein_ID, Age, Sex, Fraction, Abundance) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Fraction, values_from = Abundance) %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(Soluble), is.finite(Insoluble), Soluble > 0, Insoluble > 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Soluble_corrected =
      Soluble * ratio_sol_scale_factor,
    Insoluble_corrected =
      Insoluble * ratio_ins_scale_factor,
    log2_InsSol = log2(Insoluble_corrected / Soluble_corrected)
  )

ratio_group_mean <- ratio_sample %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID, Sex, Age) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Mean_log2_InsSol = mean(log2_InsSol, na.rm = TRUE), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

ratio_effect <- ratio_group_mean %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Age, values_from = c(Mean_log2_InsSol, n)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(Mean_log2_InsSol_Adult),
    is.finite(Mean_log2_InsSol_Old),
    n_Adult >= min_detected,
    n_Old >= min_detected
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Adult = Mean_log2_InsSol_Adult, Old = Mean_log2_InsSol_Old, Delta_InsSol = Old - Adult) %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein_ID, Sex, Adult, Old, Delta_InsSol, n_Adult, n_Old)

ratio_p <- ratio_sample %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Protein_ID, Sex) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ tibble::tibble(p_InsSol = safe_welch_p(.x, log2_InsSol))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

ratio_effect <- ratio_effect %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ratio_p, by = c("Protein_ID", "Sex"))

# Wide tables used by the consensus fate annotation heatmap.
ins_effect_wide <- ins_effect %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein_ID, Sex, Delta_Ins, p_Ins) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Sex, values_from = c(Delta_Ins, p_Ins), names_glue = "{.value}_{Sex}")

ratio_effect_wide <- ratio_effect %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein_ID, Sex, Delta_InsSol, p_InsSol) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Sex, values_from = c(Delta_InsSol, p_InsSol), names_glue = "{.value}_{Sex}")

adult_consensus_fate <- adult_consensus %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ins_presence, by = "Protein_ID") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ins_effect_wide, by = "Protein_ID") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ratio_effect_wide, by = "Protein_ID") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Adult_Ins = dplyr::coalesce(Adult_Ins, "—"), Old_Ins = dplyr::coalesce(Old_Ins, "—"))

readr::write_csv(
  adult_consensus_fate %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Protein_ID,
      Gene,
      Protein_Label,
      Bin,
      Na4vSS_percentile,
      TANGO_percentile,
      WALTZ_percentile,
      Consensus_percentile,
      Adult_Ins,
      Old_Ins,
      dplyr::starts_with("Delta_Ins_"),
      dplyr::starts_with("p_Ins_"),
      dplyr::starts_with("Delta_InsSol_"),
      dplyr::starts_with("p_InsSol_")
    ),
  file.path(nat_dirs$Fate, "Adult_Consensus_Fate.csv")
)
```

## Consensus propensity + insoluble-fate annotation heatmap

The original percentile-rank heatmap remains unchanged as a standalone output. The additional figure below places propensity rank, insoluble detection, and age-associated fate side-by-side. Detection tiles show whether the protein met the detection criterion in females (`F`), males (`M`), both (`F/M`), or neither (`—`). Continuous fate tiles show age-associated log2FC, with positive values indicating increased insoluble abundance or a shift toward greater relative insolubility. `*` denotes raw p < 0.05.

```{r adult-consensus-fate-heatmap, fig.keep="none"}
fate_order <- adult_consensus$Protein_Label

# Propensity percentile block — viridis is intentionally retained here so that
# percentile rank is visually distinct from the diverging age-effect scale.
p_prop_fate <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  adult_consensus_long,
  ggplot2::aes(x = Metric, y = Protein_Label, fill = Percentile)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = nm_style$axis_line) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", direction = 1, limits = c(0, 1), name = "Percentile rank") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_nm(legend_position = "bottom", plot_title = FALSE, plot_subtitle = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
      family = nm_style$font_family,
      size = nm_style$small_text,
      colour = "black"
    ),
    axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

presence_long <- adult_consensus_fate %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein_Label, Adult_Ins, Old_Ins) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(Adult_Ins, Old_Ins), names_to = "Stage", values_to = "Detection") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Stage = dplyr::recode(Stage, "Adult_Ins" = "Adult ins.", "Old_Ins" = "Old ins."),
    Stage = factor(Stage, levels = c("Adult ins.", "Old ins.")),
    Protein_Label = factor(Protein_Label, levels = rev(fate_order)),
    Detected = Detection != "—"
  )

p_presence <- ggplot2::ggplot(presence_long, ggplot2::aes(x = Stage, y = Protein_Label, fill = Detected)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = nm_style$axis_line) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = Detection),
    family = nm_style$font_family,
    size = nm_style$small_text / 2.845276
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "white", `TRUE` = "grey78"), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_nm(legend_position = "none", plot_title = FALSE, plot_subtitle = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(), axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank())

fate_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  adult_consensus_fate %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Protein_Label, Measure = "ΔIns F", Effect = Delta_Ins_Female, p_raw = p_Ins_Female),
  adult_consensus_fate %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Protein_Label, Measure = "ΔIns M", Effect = Delta_Ins_Male, p_raw = p_Ins_Male),
  adult_consensus_fate %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Protein_Label, Measure = "ΔIns/Sol F", Effect = Delta_InsSol_Female, p_raw = p_InsSol_Female),
  adult_consensus_fate %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Protein_Label, Measure = "ΔIns/Sol M", Effect = Delta_InsSol_Male, p_raw = p_InsSol_Male)
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Measure = factor(Measure, levels = c("ΔIns F", "ΔIns M", "ΔIns/Sol F", "ΔIns/Sol M")),
    Protein_Label = factor(Protein_Label, levels = rev(fate_order)),
    Sig = dplyr::if_else(is.finite(p_raw) & p_raw < 0.05, "*", "")
  )

fate_lim <- max(abs(fate_long$Effect), na.rm = TRUE)

if (!is.finite(fate_lim) || fate_lim == 0) {
  fate_lim <- 1
}

p_fate <- ggplot2::ggplot(fate_long, ggplot2::aes(x = Measure, y = Protein_Label, fill = Effect)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = nm_style$axis_line) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = Sig),
    family = nm_style$font_family,
    size = nm_style$stat_text / 2.845276,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "#F7F7F7",
    high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-fate_lim, fate_lim),
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Age effect\nlog2FC"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_nm(legend_position = "bottom", plot_title = FALSE, plot_subtitle = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(), axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank())

p_consensus_fate <- (p_prop_fate | p_presence | p_fate) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(3.0, 1.35, 4.0)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Fate of high-propensity Adult-soluble proteins",
    subtitle = "Detection: F, M, or F/M; continuous tiles are Old − Adult; * raw p < 0.05"
  )

p_consensus_fate_paper <- (p_prop_fate | p_presence | p_fate) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(3.0, 1.35, 4.0))

save_nat_figure(
  p_consensus_fate_paper,
  file.path(nat_dirs$Fate, "Adult_Consensus_Fate_Heatmap.svg"),
  size_key = "fate_heat"
)
```

## Adult-to-Old solubility fate of top-propensity proteins

The dumbbell plot follows the highest-ranking consensus proteins from Adult to Old muscle using mean volume-corrected log2(Insoluble/Soluble), separately in females and males. A rightward shift indicates greater relative insolubility with aging. Proteins without measurable values in both fractions at both ages are not shown in this plot; their detection fate remains represented in the heatmap above.


# Does intrinsic propensity predict an age-associated shift toward insolubility?

This analysis uses the entire Adult-soluble starting pool for which an Adult-to-Old volume-corrected log2(Insoluble/Soluble) effect can be estimated. The regression therefore tests the continuous relationship without imposing an arbitrary high-propensity cutoff. **The correlation dataset and statistical calculations are unchanged from v21.** For visualization only, each panel labels the **union** of two descriptive sets: (i) the metric-specific top 10 Adult-soluble proteins by intrinsic propensity score and (ii) the top 5 proteins with the largest positive age-associated shift toward insolubility within that sex. These labeling rules are added only after the statistics are calculated and do not alter r, p, q, or the proteins entering the regression.

```{r adult-soluble-propensity-vs-ratio-shift, fig.keep="none"}
# Visualization-only lookup: top 10 are selected independently within each metric.
# This object is joined only AFTER correlation statistics are calculated, so it
# cannot alter r, p, q, or the proteins entering the regression.
adult_top_metric_lookup <- adult_top_propensity %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Protein_ID, Metric_key = as.character(Metric), Top_metric = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

ratio_propensity <- ratio_effect %>%
  dplyr::filter(Protein_ID %in% adult_propensity$Protein_ID) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    adult_propensity %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Protein_ID,
        Gene,
        Protein_Label,
        Bin,
        Consensus_percentile,
        Na4vSS_percentile,
        TANGO_percentile,
        WALTZ_percentile
      ),
    by = "Protein_ID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(metrics_long, by = "Protein_ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(Delta_InsSol), is.finite(Metric_Score), Bin %in% display_bins) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    log2FC = Delta_InsSol,
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Metric = factor(Metric, levels = metric_levels)
  )

# IMPORTANT: statistics are calculated here, before any top-10 highlighting join.
ratio_cor_stats <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Sex, Metric) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ safe_cor_stats(.x)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Sex) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(q_BH = stats::p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Facet = paste0(
      "<b>",
      Sex,
      " — ",
      Metric,
      "</b><br><span style='font-size:5.7pt;font-weight:normal;'>",
      "r=",
      ifelse(is.na(r), "NA", sprintf("%.2f", r)),
      ", p=",
      fmt_p3(p),
      ", BH q=",
      fmt_p3(q_BH),
      "</span>"
    )
  )

facet_lookup <- ratio_cor_stats %>%
  dplyr::select(Sex, Metric, Facet)

ratio_propensity <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::left_join(facet_lookup, by = c("Sex", "Metric"))

facet_order <- ratio_cor_stats %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Metric = factor(Metric, levels = metric_levels)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Sex, Metric) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Facet)

ratio_propensity <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Facet = factor(Facet, levels = facet_order), Metric_key = as.character(Metric)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(adult_top_metric_lookup, by = c("Protein_ID", "Metric_key")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Top_metric = dplyr::coalesce(Top_metric, FALSE))

# Descriptive lookup: top age-associated increases in relative insolubility
# within each sex. This affects labeling only, not the regression statistics.
ratio_top_shift_labels <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Sex, Protein_ID, Gene, Protein_Label, Bin, Delta_InsSol) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Sex) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(order_by = Delta_InsSol, n = top_n_shift_label, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

ratio_propensity <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::left_join(

    by = c("Sex", "Protein_ID")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Top_shift = dplyr::coalesce(Top_shift, FALSE), Label_me = Top_metric | Top_shift)

# Label the union of (i) metric-specific top-10 high-propensity proteins and
# (ii) the strongest age-associated increases in the endpoint within each sex.
# These descriptive labels do NOT affect the regression.
ratio_label_data <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::filter(Label_me) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Sex, Metric, Protein_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

p_ratio_corr <- ggplot2::ggplot(ratio_propensity, ggplot2::aes(x = Delta_InsSol, y = Metric_Score)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = nm_style$axis_line, colour = "grey65") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = Bin), size = nm_style$point_small, alpha = 0.58) +
  ggplot2::geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",

  ) +

  ) +

    name = "Cellular component"
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Facet, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Adult-soluble aggregation propensity vs age-associated shift toward insolubility",
    x = "Age effect on volume-corrected log2(Insoluble/Soluble), Old − Adult",
    y = "Intrinsic aggregation propensity"
  ) +
  theme_nm(legend_position = "right") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(
      family = nm_style$font_family,
      size = nm_style$strip_text,
      lineheight = 1.02
    )
  )

# Export the exact rows used in the correlation so future versions can be

readr::write_csv(
```

# Reverse-angle analysis: aggregation propensity of the strongest age-related shifters

The analyses above start with intrinsic aggregation propensity and ask whether it predicts age-associated movement toward insolubility. This complementary descriptive analysis starts from the opposite direction. Within each sex, proteins are ranked by the magnitude of their age-associated increase and the top 10 positive shifters are then displayed across Na4vSS, TANGO, and WALTZ. The first analysis uses the **volume-corrected Δlog2(Insoluble/Soluble)** endpoint; the second uses the age-associated change in **insoluble abundance**. Selection is based only on the effect size, not on statistical significance. Raw p-values, effect sizes, cellular component, and all three propensity metrics are retained in the exported CSV files.

```{r adult-soluble-top-shifters-propensity, fig.keep="none"}
top_n_shift <- 10

top_shift_dir <- nat_dirs$TopShifters

dir.create(top_shift_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

prepare_top_shifter_data <- function(effect_data, effect_col, p_col, effect_label, top_n = 10) {

  ranked <- effect_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sex %in% c("Female", "Male"), is.finite(.data[[effect_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Protein_ID,
      Sex = factor(as.character(Sex), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
      Shift = .data[[effect_col]],
      p_raw = .data[[p_col]]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      adult_propensity %>%
        dplyr::select(
          Protein_ID,
          Gene,
          Protein_Label,
          Bin,
          Na4vSS,
          TANGO,
          `WALTZ %`,
          Na4vSS_percentile,
          TANGO_percentile,
          WALTZ_percentile,
          Consensus_percentile
        ),
      by = "Protein_ID"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Protein_Label), Bin %in% display_bins) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Sex) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Shift), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Shift_rank = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Effect = effect_label)

  top10 <- ranked %>%
    dplyr::filter(Shift > 0) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Sex) %>%
    dplyr::slice_max(order_by = Shift, n = top_n, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Sex, dplyr::desc(Shift)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Top_rank = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  top_long <- top10 %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Protein_ID,
      Gene,
      Protein_Label,
      Bin,
      Sex,
      Shift,
      p_raw,
      Top_rank,
      Consensus_percentile,
      dplyr::all_of(metric_levels)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::all_of(metric_levels), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Metric_Score") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Metric = factor(Metric, levels = metric_levels))

  list(ranked = ranked, top10 = top10, long = top_long)
}

make_top_shifter_plot <- function(plot_data, figure_title, sex_name = NULL, show_title = TRUE) {

  dd <- plot_data

  if (!is.null(sex_name)) {
    dd <- dd %>%
      dplyr::filter(as.character(Sex) == sex_name) %>%
      droplevels()
  }

  if (nrow(dd) == 0L) {
    stop("No top-shifter data available for ", ifelse(is.null(sex_name), "the combined figure", sex_name), ".")
  }

  order_tbl <- dd %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Sex, Protein_Label, Top_rank) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Sex, Top_rank) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Protein_Facet = paste0(Protein_Label, "___SEX___", as.character(Sex)))

  # Discrete y scales are ordered bottom-to-top, so reverse each sex-specific
  # ranking to place the largest shifter (rank 1) at the top.
  y_levels <- unlist(
    lapply(
      levels(droplevels(dd$Sex)),
      function(sx) {
        order_tbl %>%
          dplyr::filter(as.character(Sex) == sx) %>%
          dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Top_rank)) %>%
          dplyr::pull(Protein_Facet)
      }
    ),
    use.names = FALSE
  )

  dd <- dd %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Protein_Facet = factor(paste0(Protein_Label, "___SEX___", as.character(Sex)), levels = unique(y_levels))
    )

  vline_data <- tibble::tibble(Metric = factor("Na4vSS", levels = metric_levels))

  if (is.null(sex_name)) {
    vline_data <- tidyr::expand_grid(
      Sex = factor(c("Female", "Male"), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
      Metric = factor("Na4vSS", levels = metric_levels)
    )
  }

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(dd, ggplot2::aes(x = Metric_Score, y = Protein_Facet, colour = Bin)) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
      data = vline_data,
      ggplot2::aes(xintercept = 0),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = nm_style$axis_line,
      colour = "grey70"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = nm_style$point_rank, alpha = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
      values = adult_component_cols,
      limits = names(adult_component_cols),
      breaks = names(adult_component_cols),
      drop = FALSE,
      name = "Cellular component"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
      labels = function(x) {
        sub("___SEX___.*$", "", x)
      }
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = if (show_title) figure_title else NULL,
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      colour = "Cellular component"
    ) +
    theme_nm(legend_position = "right", plot_title = show_title, plot_subtitle = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
        family = nm_style$font_family,
        size = nm_style$small_text,
        colour = "black"
      ),
      strip.background = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
        family = nm_style$font_family,
        size = nm_style$strip_text,
        face = "bold",
        colour = "black"
      ),
      panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(4.0, "mm"),
      panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(3.0, "mm")
    )

  if (is.null(sex_name)) {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::facet_grid(
        rows = ggplot2::vars(Sex),
        cols = ggplot2::vars(Metric),
        scales = "free",
        space = "free_x"
      )
  } else {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Metric, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x")
  }

  p
}

save_top_shifter_set <- function(obj, file_tag, title_text) {

  # Full ranked table: retains every protein with an estimable sex-specific
  # age effect, not only the displayed top 10.
  readr::write_csv(obj$ranked, file.path(top_shift_dir, paste0(file_tag, "_All.csv")))

  # Compact table corresponding to the proteins displayed in the figure.
  readr::write_csv(obj$top10, file.path(top_shift_dir, paste0(file_tag, "_Top10.csv")))

  p_both <- make_top_shifter_plot(obj$long, figure_title = title_text, sex_name = NULL, show_title = TRUE)

  p_both_paper <- make_top_shifter_plot(obj$long, figure_title = title_text, sex_name = NULL, show_title = FALSE)

  save_nat_figure(p_both_paper, file.path(top_shift_dir, paste0(file_tag, "_Both.svg")), size_key = "shift_both")

  for (sx in c("Female", "Male")) {

    sx_tag <- ifelse(sx == "Female", "F", "M")

    p_sx <- make_top_shifter_plot(
      obj$long,
      figure_title = paste0(sx, " — ", title_text),
      sex_name = sx,
      show_title = TRUE
    )

    p_sx_paper <- make_top_shifter_plot(obj$long, figure_title = title_text, sex_name = sx, show_title = FALSE)

    save_nat_figure(
      p_sx_paper,
      file.path(top_shift_dir, paste0(file_tag, "_", sx_tag, ".svg")),
      size_key = "shift_sex"
    )
  }

  invisible(p_both)
}
```

# Volume-corrected Ins/Sol age effects within cellular components

This section integrates the cellular-component analysis that was previously kept in the separate `AS` workflow. It uses the **same Adult-soluble starting pool and the same volume-corrected paired log2(Insoluble/Soluble) age effects** used in the preceding analysis. Within each aggregation metric, Female and Male correlations are estimated separately inside each cellular component. A component is displayed only when both sex-specific fits are estimable (at least five proteins with nonconstant values); all attempted tests remain in the exported CSV.

```{r adult-soluble-ratio-shift-by-component, fig.keep="none"}
ratio_cc_dir <- nat_dirs$RatioCC

dir.create(ratio_cc_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ratio_cc_data <- ratio_propensity %>%
  dplyr::filter(Bin %in% display_bins, is.finite(Delta_InsSol), is.finite(Metric_Score)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Bin = factor(as.character(Bin), levels = display_bins),
    Sex = factor(as.character(Sex), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Metric = factor(as.character(Metric), levels = metric_levels)
  )

ratio_cc_stats <- ratio_cc_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Metric, Bin, Sex) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(
    ~ {
      z <- .x
      n_protein <- dplyr::n_distinct(z$Protein_ID)
      sx <- stats::sd(z$Delta_InsSol, na.rm = TRUE)
      sy <- stats::sd(z$Metric_Score, na.rm = TRUE)

      if (n_protein < 5 || !is.finite(sx) || !is.finite(sy) || sx == 0 || sy == 0) {
        return(
          tibble::tibble(n = n_protein, r = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_, status = "Not estimable")
        )
      }

      ct <- stats::cor.test(z$Delta_InsSol, z$Metric_Score, method = "pearson")

      fit <- stats::lm(Metric_Score ~ Delta_InsSol, data = z)

      tibble::tibble(
        n = n_protein,
        r = unname(ct$estimate),
        p = ct$p.value,
        slope = unname(stats::coef(fit)[["Delta_InsSol"]]),
        status = "OK"
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(q_BH = stats::p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))

readr::write_csv(ratio_cc_stats, file.path(ratio_cc_dir, "RatioCC_stats.csv"))

ratio_cc_selection <- tidyr::expand_grid(Metric = metric_levels, Bin = display_bins) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    ratio_cc_stats %>%
      dplyr::select(Metric, Bin, Sex, status) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(ok = status == "OK") %>%
      dplyr::select(-status) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Sex, values_from = ok, values_fill = FALSE),
    by = c("Metric", "Bin")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Female = dplyr::coalesce(Female, FALSE),
    Male = dplyr::coalesce(Male, FALSE),
    Include = Female & Male
  )

readr::write_csv(ratio_cc_selection, file.path(ratio_cc_dir, "RatioCC_selection.csv"))

ratio_cc_bin_tags <- c(
  "Sarcomere/Myofibril" = "Sarc",
  "Cytoskeleton" = "Cyt",
  "Extracellular" = "Ext",
  "ECM" = "ECM",
  "Nucleus" = "Nuc",
  "Mitochondrion" = "Mit",
  "Plasma membrane" = "PM",
  "Cytosol" = "Csol"
)

ratio_cc_metric_labels <- c(
  "Na4vSS" = "AGGRESCAN Na4vSS",
  "TANGO" = "TANGO / sequence length",
  "WALTZ %" = "WALTZ residues (%)"
)

make_ratio_cc_plot <- function(metric, bins_here, show_legend = TRUE, single = FALSE) {

  dd <- ratio_cc_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(as.character(Metric) == metric, as.character(Bin) %in% bins_here)

  ss <- ratio_cc_stats %>%
    dplyr::filter(as.character(Metric) == metric, as.character(Bin) %in% bins_here)

  strip_df <- ss %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      stat = paste0(Sex, ": n=", n, ", r=", ifelse(is.na(r), "NA", sprintf("%.2f", r)), ", p=", fmt_p3(p))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Bin, Sex, stat) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Sex, values_from = stat) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Strip = paste(as.character(Bin), Female, Male, sep = "\n"))

  dd <- dd %>%
    dplyr::left_join(strip_df %>% dplyr::select(Bin, Strip), by = "Bin")

  strip_levels <- strip_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Bin = factor(as.character(Bin), levels = display_bins)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Bin) %>%
    dplyr::pull(Strip)

  dd <- dd %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Strip = factor(Strip, levels = strip_levels))

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(dd, ggplot2::aes(x = Delta_InsSol, y = Metric_Score)) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey65", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = nm_style$axis_line) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = Sex, shape = Sex), size = nm_style$point_small, alpha = 0.70) +
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(
      ggplot2::aes(colour = Sex, fill = Sex, group = Sex),
      method = "lm",
      formula = y ~ x,
      se = TRUE,
      alpha = 0.12,
      linewidth = nm_style$data_line,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = sex_cols, breaks = c("Female", "Male"), name = "Sex") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = sex_cols, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = sex_shapes, breaks = c("Female", "Male"), name = "Sex") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Strip, ncol = if (single) 1 else 3, nrow = if (single) 1 else 2, scales = "free") +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = if (single) {
        "Age effect on volume-corrected log2(Ins/Sol), Old − Adult"
      } else {
        "Age effect on log2(Ins/Sol): Old − Adult"
      },
      y = unname(ratio_cc_metric_labels[[metric]])
    ) +
    theme_nm(legend_position = if (show_legend) "bottom" else "none", plot_title = FALSE, plot_subtitle = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
        family = nm_style$font_family,
        size = nm_style$strip_text,
        lineheight = 1.05,
        face = "plain",
        colour = "black"
      )
    )

  p
}

for (metric in metric_levels) {

  chosen <- ratio_cc_selection %>%
    dplyr::filter(Metric == metric, Include) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Bin = factor(Bin, levels = display_bins)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Bin) %>%
    dplyr::pull(Bin) %>%
    as.character()

  if (length(chosen) == 0L) {
    next
  }

  mtag <- metric_tag(metric)

  # Individual components for flexible manuscript / extended-data assembly.
  for (bin_name in chosen) {

    btag <- unname(ratio_cc_bin_tags[[bin_name]])

    if (is.null(btag) || is.na(btag)) {
      btag <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", bin_name)
    }

    p_one <- make_ratio_cc_plot(metric = metric, bins_here = bin_name, show_legend = FALSE, single = TRUE)

    save_nat_figure(
      p_one,
      file.path(ratio_cc_dir, mtag, paste0("RCC_", mtag, "_", btag, ".svg")),
      size_key = "ratio_cc_single",
      save_legend = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Paginated 2 x 3 grids, matching the previous AS analysis.
  page_id <- ceiling(seq_along(chosen) / 6)

  for (page in sort(unique(page_id))) {

    page_bins <- chosen[page_id == page]

    p_grid <- make_ratio_cc_plot(metric = metric, bins_here = page_bins, show_legend = TRUE, single = FALSE)

    p_grid_svg <- p_grid

    save_nat_figure(
      p_grid_svg,
      file.path(ratio_cc_dir, mtag, paste0("RCC_", mtag, "_grid", page, ".svg")),
      size_key = "ratio_cc_grid"
    )
  }
}
```

# Intrinsic aggregation propensity across cellular components — Adult and Old analyzed separately

This analysis does **not pool Adult and Old proteins**. Control animals are analyzed separately within each age group, but female and male detections are pooled for eligibility. Within an age, a protein is retained when it is detected in **at least 2 Control soluble samples total regardless of sex** and is represented once per cellular component and aggregation metric, because AGGRESCAN, TANGO, and WALTZ are intrinsic sequence-derived properties of the protein.

```{r age-specific-go-component-propensity, fig.keep="none"}
component_order <- rev(display_bins)

all_bins_palette <- sort(unique(as.character(long$Bin[long$Bin != "Other/Unassigned"])))

component_pal_all <- setNames(
  viridisLite::viridis(length(all_bins_palette), option = "D", end = 0.95),
  all_bins_palette
)

component_cols <- component_pal_all[display_bins]

# Keep Adult and Old separate from the outset, but define each age-specific
# soluble protein universe WITHOUT sex stratification. A protein group enters an
# age-specific universe when it is detected in >= 2 Control soluble samples total
# across females and males. This matches the relaxed criterion used for the Adult
# protein-level landscape. The protein is counted only once because propensity is
# sequence-derived.
age_component_pool_counts <- long %>%
  dplyr::filter(Treatment == "Control", Age %in% c("Adult", "Old"), Bin %in% display_bins) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Age, Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(N_detected = sum(Detected, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::filter(N_detected >= min_detected) %>%
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(Protein.Group, delim = ";") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Protein_ID = clean_id(Protein.Group)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Protein_ID != "",
    !stringr::str_detect(Protein_ID, stringr::regex("^cRAP-", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Age, Protein_ID, Bin, N_detected)

readr::write_csv(age_component_pool_counts, file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, "Age_GO_pool_detection_audit.csv"))

age_component_metric <- age_component_pool_counts %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(metrics_long, by = "Protein_ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Age, Protein_ID, Bin, Metric, Metric_Score) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Age = factor(Age, levels = c("Adult", "Old")),
    Bin = factor(as.character(Bin), levels = component_order)
  )

# QC: number of unique proteins contributing to each age × component × metric.
age_component_n <- age_component_metric %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Age, Metric, Bin) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(N_proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(Protein_ID), .groups = "drop")

readr::write_csv(age_component_n, file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, "Age_GO_N.csv"))

run_age_component_tests <- function(age_name) {

  dd_age <- age_component_metric %>%
    dplyr::filter(Age == age_name) %>%
    droplevels()

  kw <- dd_age %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Metric) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(
      function(.x, .y) {

        dd <- .x %>%
          dplyr::group_by(Bin) %>%
          dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Protein_ID) >= min_go_n) %>%
          dplyr::ungroup() %>%
          droplevels()

        if (dplyr::n_distinct(dd$Bin) < 2) {
          return(tibble::tibble(p_KW = NA_real_))
        }

        tibble::tibble(p_KW = stats::kruskal.test(Metric_Score ~ Bin, data = dd)$p.value)
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Age = age_name, .before = 1)

  dunn <- dd_age %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Metric) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(
      function(.x, .y) {

        dd <- .x %>%
          dplyr::group_by(Bin) %>%
          dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Protein_ID) >= min_go_n) %>%
          dplyr::ungroup() %>%
          droplevels()

        if (dplyr::n_distinct(dd$Bin) < 2) {
          return(tibble::tibble())
        }

        rstatix::dunn_test(dd, Metric_Score ~ Bin, p.adjust.method = "holm")
      }
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Age = age_name, .before = 1)

  list(kw = kw, dunn = dunn)
}

adult_component_tests <- run_age_component_tests("Adult")

old_component_tests <- run_age_component_tests("Old")

readr::write_csv(adult_component_tests$kw, file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, "Adult_GO_KW.csv"))

readr::write_csv(adult_component_tests$dunn, file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, "Adult_GO_Dunn.csv"))

readr::write_csv(old_component_tests$kw, file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, "Old_GO_KW.csv"))

readr::write_csv(old_component_tests$dunn, file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, "Old_GO_Dunn.csv"))

make_age_component_plot <- function(age_name, metric, show_component_labels = TRUE) {

  test_obj <- if (age_name == "Adult") {
    adult_component_tests
  } else {
    old_component_tests
  }

  dd <- age_component_metric %>%
    dplyr::filter(Age == age_name, Metric == metric) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Bin) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Protein_ID) >= min_go_n) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    droplevels()

  kw_p <- test_obj$kw %>%
    dplyr::filter(Metric == metric) %>%
    dplyr::pull(p_KW)

  sig_dunn <- test_obj$dunn %>%
    dplyr::filter(Metric == metric, !is.na(p.adj), p.adj <= 0.05) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(p_label = paste0("p=", fmt_p3(p.adj)))

  if (nrow(sig_dunn) > 0) {

    score_range <- range(dd$Metric_Score, na.rm = TRUE)

    score_span <- diff(score_range)

    if (!is.finite(score_span) || score_span <= 0) {
      score_span <- 1
    }

    bracket_step <- if (metric == "Na4vSS") {
      0.12 * score_span
    } else {
      0.08 * score_span
    }

    sig_dunn <- sig_dunn %>%
      dplyr::arrange(p.adj, group1, group2) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(y.position = max(dd$Metric_Score, na.rm = TRUE) + seq_len(dplyr::n()) * bracket_step)
  }

  score_range <- range(dd$Metric_Score, na.rm = TRUE)

  score_span <- diff(score_range)

  if (!is.finite(score_span) || score_span <= 0) {
    score_span <- 1
  }

  upper_bound <- if (nrow(sig_dunn) > 0) {
    max(sig_dunn$y.position, na.rm = TRUE) +
      0.08 * score_span
  } else {
    score_range[2] +
      0.08 * score_span
  }

  lower_bound <- score_range[1] -
    0.05 * score_span

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(dd, ggplot2::aes(x = Bin, y = Metric_Score, fill = Bin)) +
    ggplot2::geom_violin(trim = (metric == "WALTZ %"), alpha = 0.35, colour = NA, scale = "width") +
      ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.10, height = 0, size = nm_style$point_small, alpha = 0.15, colour = "black") +
    ggplot2::geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85, linewidth = nm_style$data_line) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = component_cols, drop = FALSE)

  if (nrow(sig_dunn) > 0) {
    p <- p +
      ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(
        sig_dunn,
        label = "p_label",
        xmin = "group1",
        xmax = "group2",
        y.position = "y.position",
        tip.length = 0.01,
        bracket.size = nm_style$axis_line,
        size = 2.1,
        hide.ns = TRUE,
        coord.flip = TRUE,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
  }

  p +
    ggplot2::coord_flip(ylim = c(lower_bound, upper_bound), clip = "on") +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = metric,
      subtitle = paste0(age_name, ": Kruskal-Wallis p = ", fmt_p3(kw_p)),
      x = NULL,
      y = metric_y_labels[[metric]]
    ) +
    theme_nm(legend_position = "none") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        family = nm_style$font_family,
        face = "bold",
        size = nm_style$plot_title,
        hjust = 0.5
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(
        family = nm_style$font_family,
        size = nm_style$stat_text,
        hjust = 0.5,
        colour = "black"
      ),
      axis.text.y = if (show_component_labels) {
        ggplot2::element_text(family = nm_style$font_family, size = nm_style$axis_text, colour = "black")
      } else {
        ggplot2::element_blank()
      },
      axis.ticks.y = if (show_component_labels) {
        ggplot2::element_line(linewidth = nm_style$axis_line)
      } else {
        ggplot2::element_blank()
      }
    )
}

make_age_3metric_figure <- function(age_name) {

  plots <- list(
    make_age_component_plot(age_name, "Na4vSS", TRUE),
    make_age_component_plot(age_name, "TANGO", FALSE),
    make_age_component_plot(age_name, "WALTZ %", FALSE)
  )

  patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1)
}

# Save individual metric plots and one 3-metric figure for Adult and Old separately.
for (age_name in c("Adult", "Old")) {

  age_tag <- ifelse(age_name == "Adult", "Adult", "Old")

  for (metric in metric_levels) {

    p_ind <- make_age_component_plot(age_name, metric, TRUE)

    save_nat_figure(
      p_ind,
      file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, paste0(age_tag, "_GO_", metric_tag(metric), ".svg")),
      size_key = "go_single"
    )
  }

  p_combined <- make_age_3metric_figure(age_name)

  save_nat_figure(
    p_combined,
    file.path(nat_dirs$GOComponents, paste0(age_tag, "_GO_3metric.svg")),
    size_key = "go_three"
  )
}
```
